sections.h2: Where is Oregon City, and why does its terrain matter?
sections.html:
Oregon City is the county seat of Clackamas County, on the Willamette River near the southern edge of the Portland metro area. The city sits at 466 feet and is built in two tiers: a lower area on a bench beside the river and an upper area on a basalt bluff.

The Willamette forms the boundary with West Linn, and the Clackamas River forms the boundary with Gladstone. A water-powered elevator linked the two tiers in 1915, was converted to electricity in the 1920s and replaced by a new electric elevator in 1952. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. If your house is on the bluff, say so, since buyers care about slope, views and walking access.

sections.h2: Which Oregon City neighborhoods come up most?
sections.html:
The city lists 12 official neighborhood associations. Three areas stand out in descriptions of the city.

  • McLoughlin sits on the bluff above downtown and has many older homes, the McLoughlin House, the public library, a pool and a hospital.
  • Canemah is a narrow strip between the Willamette and a bluff along OR 99E. It was founded in 1845 as an independent city, served as the portage site around the falls, and was later annexed.
  • Two Rivers is the lowest part of the city and mostly commercial, including downtown and Clackamette Park.

Oregon City was the end of the Oregon Trail and the first U.S. city west of the Rocky Mountains to incorporate. Dr. John McLoughlin of the Hudson's Bay Company founded the settlement in 1829 to use Willamette Falls to power a lumber mill, and the city incorporated in 1844.

  • It was the capital of Oregon Territory from 1848 to 1851.
  • The Oregon Spectator, published in 1846, was the first American newspaper west of the Rockies.
  • In 1889 the city began the first long-distance electrical service in the country, sending power 14 miles to Portland.
  • The Willamette Falls Locks, in West Linn, were the first multi-lift navigational locks in the U.S.

sections.h2: How big is Oregon City, and who lives there?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 38,175 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 37,572 in the 2020 census. In 2020 there were 13,966 households and the median age was 38.2.

Oregon City's 65.3% ownership rate and $555,800 median home value are higher than the McMinnville, Medford and Newberg figures, and only 14.7% of its residents are 65 or older.

sections.h2: What does the Oregon City economy rely on?
sections.html:
Forestry dominated the city's history until the Pacific Northwest lumber industry declined starting in the 1980s, and today Oregon City is largely a Portland suburb. The last paper mill in the immediate area closed in 2017 and reopened in 2019 under new ownership.

Tourism built on history is growing, centered on the Willamette Falls Legacy Project, a planned public-access, mixed-use redevelopment of the falls area. Clackamas Community College is in the city. The End of the Oregon Trail Interpretive Center closed in September 2009 over funding and reopened in summer 2013. Other sites include the Museum of the Oregon Territory, the 1908 Stevens-Crawford Heritage House Museum, the Ermatinger House, the oldest in Clackamas County, and the 1922 Oregon City Bridge.

sections.h2: What does the weather mean for an Oregon City house?
sections.html:
Oregon City has hot, dry summers and cool, wet winters, with most of its 44.81 inches of annual rain falling from November to March. The annual average temperature is 55.4 degrees, and December averages 41.8.

The record high is 114 degrees, set June 28, 2021, and the record low is minus 2, on January 31, 1950. A wet half of the year is hard on roofs, decks and retaining walls, and bluff lots add drainage to the list of things a buyer will check.

sections.h2: How do roads, trains and buses serve Oregon City?
sections.html:
Interstate 205 crosses the northern edge of the city and is the only freeway serving it. Oregon Routes 43, 99E and 213 pass through or end in town.

  • Amtrak Cascades trains stop twice daily in each direction between Portland and Eugene, while the Coast Starlight passes without stopping.
  • TriMet buses converge at the Oregon City Transit Center, with added service from South Clackamas Transportation District and Canby Area Transit.
  • There is no public airport in the city. Portland International is about 15 miles north.

The Oregon City School District has seven elementary schools, two middle schools, Oregon City High School and an alternative secondary school. Several schools offer bilingual English and Spanish programs. Oregon City High School is described as the third most populated high school in Oregon.

sections.h2: What do Oregon City historic districts mean for a seller?
sections.html:
If your house is in a designated historic area, exterior changes need city review before work starts. Oregon City's list includes the Canemah National Register District and the McLoughlin Conservation District, which spans streets from 1st through 12th.

  • Windows, doors, siding changes and additions to designated structures need special review.
  • Type I review is a staff decision for limited alterations that meet clear policies.
  • Type III review goes to the Historic Review Board for discretionary decisions, additions under 30% of the original structure, and new construction or larger additions.

Planning staff can say whether a property is designated at ocplanning@orcity.org or 503-722-3789. A buyer who plans changes will ask, so find out before you list.

sections.h2: How are Clackamas County property taxes billed for an Oregon City house?
sections.html:
Clackamas County's Department of Assessment and Taxation bills Oregon City property from its office at 150 Beavercreek Road, Suite 135, phone 503-655-8671. For 2025 it issued 170,621 statements totaling $1,235,352,377, up 5.02% from the prior year.

State law sets installments for November 15, February 15 and May 15. In 2025 the county listed the first deadline as November 17, with a 3% discount for payment in full and 2% for two-thirds, and the later installments February 17, 2026 and May 15, 2026. Value appeals went to the Property Value Appeals Board by December 31, 2025. Ask the title company to settle the current installment at closing.

sections.h2: What disclosure and sale rules should an Oregon City seller know?
sections.html:
Sellers of one-to-four-unit homes generally must give a signed disclosure statement to each buyer who makes a written offer, and a buyer has five business days after delivery to revoke unless they waived that right. Court-appointed sellers, such as personal representatives and trustees, and foreclosing financial institutions are excluded under ORS 105.470.

Oregon City sellers weigh a listing, a sale on their own and an as-is cash sale. A cash buyer sets its own terms, so compare timelines, repair responsibility and closing costs in writing.

faqs.q: What county is Oregon City in?
faqs.a: Clackamas County. Oregon City is the county seat, and the county's assessment and taxation office is in the city.

faqs.q: How many people live in Oregon City?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 38,175 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 37,572.

faqs.q: Why is Oregon City important in Oregon history?
faqs.a: It was the end of the Oregon Trail, the first U.S. city west of the Rockies to incorporate in 1844, and capital of Oregon Territory from 1848 to 1851.

faqs.q: Do Oregon City historic district rules affect selling?
faqs.a: They can. Exterior changes to designated structures need staff or Historic Review Board review, so a buyer who wants to alter a Canemah or McLoughlin house will ask about it.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Clackamas County?
faqs.a: State law sets November 15, February 15 and May 15. In 2025 the county listed November 17 for the first deadline, with a 3% discount for payment in full.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Oregon City?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimate for owner-occupied units is $555,800. It is a city-wide median, not a value for one house.
